summary: Jan E. M. Houben works in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He held posts at the Netherlands Organisation for Scientific Research (attested 1999), Leiden University (attested 2000-2002), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 2009-2012).

Jan Fontein (1927-2017) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Leiden University under Theodoor Paul Galestin, and worked at the Rijksmuseum, the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, and the Royal Ontario Museum.

Jan Gonda (1905-1991) worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Utrecht University under Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff, Willem Caland, and Theodorus Willem Juynboll, and at Leiden University. He held the Chair of Sanskrit and Indology at Utrecht.

Jan Jakob Maria de Groot (1854-1921) specialized in Sinology and religious studies. He studied at Leiden University and under Georg von der Gabelentz, later serving as professor at Leiden University (1891-1912) and Professor of Sinology at the University of Berlin (~1912-1921).

Jan Jaworski (1903-1945) was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Warsaw from approximately 1923 to 1928 under Stanisław Schayer, and later studied under Jean Przyluski (~1928-1930).

Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak (1889-1954) was a Sinologist who studied at Leiden University, the Sorbonne, and the University of Berlin under scholars including Jan Jakob Maria de Groot. He was a professor of Chinese language and literature at Leiden University (1930-1954).

Jan N. Bremmer (born 1944) specializes in religious studies, history, and archaeology. He earned degrees from Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, the University of Bristol, and the University of Amsterdam, and served as Chair of Religious Studies at the University of Groningen (1990-2009).

Jan Nattier (born 1949) specializes in Buddhist studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology. She studied at Indiana University and Harvard University, where Masatoshi Nagatomi supervised her PhD, and held faculty posts at Macalester College, Indiana University, and Soka University.

Jan Peter F. Hintelmann works in Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg under doctoral supervisor Marianne Pieper, and studied under traditional teachers Thupten Nyandak, Tenzin Kunga, Sonam Senge, and Geshe Sonam Rinchen.

Jan Pieter Hogendijk (born 1955) is a historian of mathematics. He earned his doctorate at Utrecht University and studied under G. J. Toomer, later holding professorial posts in the history of mathematics at Leiden University and Utrecht University.

Jan Westerhoff (born 1976) works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Michael Potter and also studied at SOAS. His posts include lecturer at Durham University and Professor of Buddhist Philosophy at Oxford.

Jan Willem de Jong (1921-2000) was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and Tibetologist. He completed his PhD at Leiden University and studied at the Sorbonne and Collège de France. He held posts at Leiden University and the Australian National University.

Jan-Ulrich Sobisch works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctorate under David P. Jackson and studied with David Seyfort Ruegg and Nubpa Rinpoche. He has held posts at the universities of Hamburg, Munich, and Copenhagen (2003-2006).
Janakiballav Bhattacharyya was an Indologist and philosopher who studied as a pupil of Surendranath Dasgupta. He held an attested post at Jadavpur University in 1977.

Janardan Mishra worked in Indology and philosophy. He served as Director of the Mithila Institute of Post-Graduate Studies and Research in Sanskrit Learning, with his tenure attested in 1959 and 1987.

Jane Bunnag is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at University College London in 1969, where she studied under the supervision of E. Michael Mendelson and Barbara E. Ward.

Jane Ellen Harrison (1850-1928) was a scholar in religious studies, history, and archaeology. She studied at Cheltenham Ladies' College and Newnham College, learning under Robert Alexander Neil, and held a post at the University of Cambridge (~1898-1922).

Janet Gyatso (born 1949) is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her BA, MA, and PhD at UC Berkeley, and held posts at Amherst College and Harvard University, where she was appointed Hershey Professor of Buddhist Studies.

Janet R. Goodwin specializes in Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Britten Dean and earned her doctorate under Delmer M. Brown at UC Berkeley, later holding positions at the University of Southern California and the University of Aizu.

Jang-Kil Chun is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. They completed doctoral studies under supervisor Minoru Kiyota and also studied under Paul J. Griffiths, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and Frances A. Wilson.
